title: GLB/glTF loading into the mesh pipeline
description: Bridge Assimp into the geometry pipeline so the ten Trellis2 scans in ~/crawfish (IMG_4109..IMG_4118.glb, one mesh each, ~623k vertices / ~936k triangles, POSITION+NORMAL+TEXCOORD_0, one PBR material, two embedded PNGs) load as HalfEdgeMesh/ArrayMesh geometry. Today MeshLoader.load dispatches only .obj/.ply/.off to parsers that emit ArrayMesh, while AssimpModelImporter (graphics/render/model) already reads GLB via lwjgl-assimp but emits GPU-interleaved floats and is reachable only from ModelLoadScene. Add a GltfMeshParser in geometry/mesh/data/load that calls Assimp.aiImportFile (aiProcess_Triangulate | aiProcess_JoinIdenticalVertices) and produces the same ArrayMesh shape as ObjMeshParser, carrying TEXCOORD_0 as a per-vertex GeometryBundle slot whose name constant lives on the parser (the material/texture bytes are CRAW-3's job). Register .glb/.gltf in MeshLoader.load, LoadMeshNode.socketDocs, ModelCatalog (staging scan and a plain directory scan) and ixdar-cli list-meshes. Loading must go through the Platform abstraction where it touches native buffers (IxBuffer, not org.lwjgl.BufferUtils). Desktop-only: the web build must not reach Assimp. Related: VIEW-6 (model staging directory + sync-models) is the catalog this extends.
definition-of-done: 1. MeshLoader.load("~/crawfish/IMG_4109.glb") returns an ArrayMesh with 622652 vertices and 936035 triangles and a UV slot of matching length. 2. `load_mesh(path="...glb")` works in a .dsl graph and mesh-viewer shows the crawfish via `uv run ixdar-cli run-scene --scene mesh-viewer --property ixdar.model=<path>`. 3. `ixdar-cli list-meshes` lists .glb files found in $IXDAR_MODEL_DIR and ~/crawfish when pointed at it. 4. Peak heap while loading one scan stays under 2 GB (no per-vertex boxing; direct buffers reused). 5. The TeaVM build (`./tools/teavm-build.sh`) still succeeds with no Assimp symbols in classes.js. 6. `mvn -q clean compile -pl annotations,ixdar-app` is checkstyle-green and all existing mesh tests pass.
testing-plan: 1. Unit test GltfMeshParserTest with a tiny hand-written .gltf (two triangles, UVs) under test resources -- asserts positions, indices, UV slot. 2. Benchmark in ixdar-app/test/benchmark/ that loads one crawfish scan and prints vertex/face counts and elapsed ms. 3. run-scene screenshot of mesh-viewer with the scan; compare against `ixdar-cli mesh-state` counts. 4. Confirm MeshLoader still rejects unknown extensions with the existing IllegalArgumentException message.
